name: sdhci_fdt_gpio_get_readonly
prose: Returns whether the SD slot is write protected according to the FDT-described write-protect GPIO; int result. If gpio->wp_disabled is set it returns false. If gpio->wp_pin is NULL it returns the value of sdhci_generic_get_ro(gpio->slot->bus, gpio->slot->dev). Otherwise it calls gpio_pin_is_active(gpio->wp_pin, &pinstate), ignoring its return value, and returns pinstate XOR gpio->wp_inverted (so pinstate is used even if the GPIO call failed and left it unset). It takes no locks.
note: sdhci_fdt_gpio.c:250-263 (packet name sdhci_gpio_get_ro does not exist; real name sdhci_fdt_gpio_get_readonly). Returns 255, 258, 262. Not read: sdhci_generic_get_ro, gpio_pin_is_active.

name: ef10_ev_rx_packed_stream
prose: Handles one packed-stream (or equal-stride super-buffer) Rx event; static boolean_t returning the callback's abort flag. It extracts the low bits of the global packet counter, the queue label and the ROTATE (new buffer) bit, and selects eersp = &eep->ee_rxq_state[label]. It computes pkt_count as (pkt_count_lbits - eers_rx_stream_npackets) masked with the ESF_DZ_RX_DSC_PTR_LBITS field mask and adds it to eers_rx_stream_npackets. If the event has the new-buffer bit it sets EFX_PKT_PACKED_STREAM_NEW_BUFFER in flags, increments eers_rx_packed_stream_credits only when EFSYS_OPT_RX_PACKED_STREAM is compiled in, and increments eers_rx_read_ptr. current_id is eers_rx_read_ptr masked with eers_rx_mask. A truncation error or an Ethernet CRC error counts the matching statistic, sets EFX_DISCARD and delivers; an incomplete parse sets EFX_PKT_PACKED_STREAM_PARSE_INCOMPLETE and delivers; otherwise IPv4 header and TCP/UDP checksum errors only count statistics. At deliver it counts EV_RX_OK when EFX_DISCARD is not set, asserts eecp->eec_rx_ps is non-NULL (EFSYS_ASSERT), calls eecp->eec_rx_ps(arg, label, current_id, pkt_count, flags) and returns its result.
note: ef10_ev.c:771-858 (compiled only with EFSYS_OPT_RX_PACKED_STREAM || EFSYS_OPT_RX_ES_SUPER_BUFFER). Reviewer round 1 right that the read-pointer index is masked with eers_rx_mask (821) and the packet counter with the LBITS mask (801-802); round 15 right that the credits increment is conditional on EFSYS_OPT_RX_PACKED_STREAM (807-818) and happens only when the new-buffer bit is set.

name: ef10_ev_rx
prose: Handles a regular EF10 Rx completion event; static boolean_t returning whether the event loop should abort. It counts EV_RX and returns B_FALSE at once, without calling the Rx callback, if enp->en_reset_flags has EFX_RESET_RXQ_ERR, EFX_RESET_TXQ_ERR or EFX_RESET_HW_UNAVAIL. It takes the queue label and eersp = &eep->ee_rxq_state[label]. When packed-stream or super-buffer support is compiled in and eersp->eers_rx_packed_stream is set it returns ef10_ev_rx_packed_stream(...) before any other decoding (so the drop-event check below does not apply to those queues). Otherwise it decodes the byte count, continuation bit, descriptor-pointer low bits and the ethernet/L3/L4 classes; if ESF_DZ_RX_DROP_EVENT is set it returns B_FALSE (no callback). It sets EFX_PKT_CONT for a continued event and EFX_PKT_UNICAST for a unicast MAC class, advances eers_rx_read_ptr by the number of descriptors consumed (modulo the LBITS mask) and, when more than one descriptor was consumed, counts EV_RX_BATCH and sets EFX_PKT_PREFIX_LEN. last_used_id is (read_ptr - 1) & eers_rx_mask. A truncation error or CRC error counts the statistic, sets EFX_DISCARD and delivers; an incomplete hardware parse delivers without further classification; otherwise it sets EFX_PKT_VLAN_TAGGED for VLAN tag classes, classifies IPv4 and IPv6 (setting EFX_PKT_IPV4/IPV6, EFX_CKSUM_IPV4 when the IP checksum is good, EFX_PKT_TCP or EFX_PKT_UDP from the L4 class, and counting statistics) and sets EFX_CKSUM_TCPUDP for TCP or UDP without a checksum error. At deliver it counts EV_RX_OK when not discarded, asserts eecp->eec_rx is non-NULL and returns the result of eecp->eec_rx(arg, label, last_used_id, size, flags).
note: ef10_ev.c:863-1072. Returns 889, 901, 925, 1071. Reviewer round 1 right (returns the callback's should_abort, not B_FALSE, 1069-1071); round 15 right (packed-stream dispatch at 900-901 precedes the drop-event test at 923, so packed-stream drop events are not returned B_FALSE here). Not read: the callback, ef10_ev_rx_packed_stream details (separate record).

name: ef10_filter_reconfigure
prose: Reconfigures all EF10 unicast, multicast and encapsulated hardware filters; returns an efx_rc_t. The caller is expected to serialize access to the filter table. If table->eft_default_rxq is NULL it deletes every unicast, multicast and encapsulation filter with ef10_filter_delete_internal (ignoring errors), sets their counts to 0 and returns 0. Otherwise it marks all existing unicast, multicast and encapsulation filters as auto-old, sets the unicast count to 0, inserts the specific unicast filter for mac_addr and, if all_unicst is true or that insertion failed, inserts the all-unicast filter; if both insertions failed it goes to fail1. It then calls ef10_filter_get_workarounds (an error goes to fail2). If the all-multicast setting changed (table->eft_using_all_mulcst != all_mulcst) and the bug26807 workaround is enabled it removes the old filters first. For all_mulcst true it inserts the all-multicast filter, and if that fails inserts the multicast list without rollback (failure goes to fail3). For all_mulcst false it inserts the multicast list with rollback; on failure it removes old filters when the workaround is enabled and all-multicast was not in use, tries the all-multicast filter, and if that also fails tries the multicast list without rollback (failure goes to fail4). When tunnel encapsulation is supported it inserts encapsulation filters, ignoring errors; it removes the remaining auto-old filters, and returns ENOTSUP if all_unicst was requested and the all-unicast insertion failed or all_mulcst was requested and the all-multicast insertion failed, otherwise the value of rc (0 on the paths reached). The fail labels clear the auto-old mark on every entry that has it (they do not delete those entries) and return rc.
note: ef10_filter.c:1532-1747 (packet name 'filter-table restore'; prose matches ef10_filter_reconfigure; slice 1550-1793 starts inside). Returns 1575, 1729, 1747. Old prose had the fail-path wording 'after clearing all auto-old marks' right; nothing contradicted. The ENOTSUP condition concerns only the all-unicast or all-multicast insertions failing (1724-1727).

name: efx_build_signed_image_write_buffer
prose: Builds the NVRAM partition layout for a signed image in a caller buffer; returns 0 or an errno. It returns EINVAL if bufferp or infop or headerpp is NULL or buffer_size is 0, if infop is not EFX_IMAGE_FORMAT_SIGNED with a non-NULL image and header, if the header lies before the image or the image is too small, or if any of the located source chunks (CMS header, image header, code, trailer, signature) does not fit within buffer_size by the size/offset check. It then fills the buffer with 0xFF and writes, in the partition order, a chunk header followed by the copied data for the reflash trailer, the CMS header, the reflash header (setting *headerpp to the copy of the image header inside the buffer), the code, and the signature; ENOSPC is returned if the buffer cannot hold a chunk header or a chunk's data (the checks before each copy), in which case the buffer may be partly written and *headerpp may or may not have been set. It takes no locks and the caller keeps ownership of the buffer.
note: ef10_image.c:603-903 (packet name '<unnamed> signed-image layout builder'). Reviewer round 17 wrong: the source-chunk checks at 642-677 return EINVAL (fail3-fail7) while the ENOSPC returns are in the later write phase (741, 756, 768, 781, 795, 808, 826, 834, 846, 859). Old prose described this correctly. The exact chunk order was taken from the header comment diagram and the copy sequence; order of the first two copies (trailer vs CMS) not verified line by line. PARTLY READ: 700-865 via control-flow lines.

name: ef10_mac_stats_update
prose: Reads the MAC statistics from the DMA stats buffer into stat[]; returns 0 or an errno. Parameters: enp, esmp (stats DMA memory), stat (array of EFX_MAC_NSTATS counters), generationp (optional). It returns ENOSPC if encp->enc_mac_stats_nstats is smaller than MC_CMD_MAC_NSTATS or the buffer is smaller than nstats 64-bit counters. Otherwise it syncs the buffer for the kernel, reads the generation-end counter from the last counter (index nstats - 1), then reads every counter group the firmware reports (extra groups only when nstats is at least the V3 or V4 count) into stat[] with EFSYS_STAT_SET_QWORD, re-syncs and reads the generation-start counter (MC_CMD_MAC_GENERATION_START). If start and end differ it returns EAGAIN (the stat[] array has already been written by then); otherwise it stores the low dword of the generation-start counter in *generationp when generationp is non-NULL and returns 0.
note: ef10_mac.c:603-1059 (packet name 'ef10_mac_stats_update (name truncated)' exists in the file; slice 1029-1064 is its tail, so fixed instead of dropped). The old (dropped) prose wrongly said the caller passes a pre-captured generation_end and that read failures return negative codes: the function reads generation_end itself (646-647) and its only failures are ENOSPC (634, 640, via fail1/fail2) and EAGAIN. PARTLY READ: the long per-counter read list 650-1034 via skim only.

name: efx_bootcfg_write
prose: Writes a DHCP-format boot configuration block into this function's sector of the BOOTROM_CFG NVRAM partition; returns 0 or an errno. The sector number is enc_pf on Huntington-family adapters and 0 otherwise. It gets the partition size (efx_nvram_size) and the sector offset and length (efx_bootcfg_sector_info), limits the sector length to BOOTCFG_MAX_SIZE, and returns EFBIG if the sector would end beyond the partition. It verifies data with efx_dhcp_verify (returning its error) and requires the verified block to be at least 2 bytes with its last byte equal to EFX_DHCP_END (ENOENT otherwise) and no longer than MIN(sector_length, BOOTCFG_MAX_SIZE) (ENOSPC otherwise). It allocates a buffer for the whole partition (ENOMEM on failure), starts a read-write NVRAM session, reads the whole partition into the buffer, zeroes the sector region, copies the block in, subtracts the block checksum from the first byte of the sector, erases the partition, writes the buffer back and finishes the session, then frees the buffer and returns 0. Errors after the session started finish the session and free the buffer; errors before it only return the code.
note: efx_bootcfg.c:1012-1145 (packet slice starts inside; name is correct). Reviewer round 15 right: the function itself checks and returns ENOENT/ENOSPC/verify errors, so the old precondition that data is already verified was wrong. The failure paths: fail12..fail9 finish the rw session (fail9 only runs it for read, erase and write failures; for fail12 the rw_finish itself failed), fail8 and later free the buffer as listed at 1116-1145. Not read: callee bodies.

name: sfxge_ev_qpoll
prose: Polls an event queue and re-primes it; returns 0 or an errno. It takes the event queue lock. If evq->init_state is neither SFXGE_EVQ_STARTING nor SFXGE_EVQ_STARTED it unlocks and returns EINVAL without touching the queue. Otherwise it syncs the event memory (POSTREAD), asserts (KASSERT) that rx_done, tx_done and txq are clear, calls efx_ev_qpoll(evq->common, &evq->read_ptr, &sfxge_ev_callbacks, evq), which can advance read_ptr, resets rx_done and tx_done to 0, calls sfxge_ev_qcomplete(evq, B_TRUE) to complete the pending Rx and Tx work, then calls efx_ev_qprime(evq->common, evq->read_ptr). If the prime fails it unlocks and returns that error, with the polled events already consumed, read_ptr advanced and the completions already done; otherwise it unlocks and returns 0.
note: sfxge_ev.c:673-713. Reviewer original right (the efx_ev_qprime failure leaves read_ptr/completion state changed, 695-704); round 15 right (init_state other than STARTING/STARTED returns EINVAL at 679-682, not a precondition). Not read: efx_ev_qpoll, sfxge_ev_qcomplete bodies.

name: tso_fill_packet_with_fragment
prose: Adds one DMA descriptor for the current TSO fragment to the transmit queue's pending list; static void. Precondition: txq and tso are valid; the in_len and packet_space values are non-negative. If tso->in_len or tso->packet_space is 0 it returns without doing anything. It saves dma_addr = tso->dma_addr before updating the state. For firmware-assisted TSO v2 (SFXGE_FATSOV2) it takes n = tso->in_len, subtracts n from out_len, adds n to seqnum, sets in_len to 0, and either (n < packet_space) decreases packet_space by n and decrements segs_space, or recomputes packet_space as seg_size - (n - packet_space) % seg_size and segs_space as EFX_TX_FATSOV2_DMA_SEGS_PER_PKT_MAX - 1 minus 1 if packet_space is not a whole seg_size; tso->dma_addr is not changed in that mode. Otherwise it takes n = min(in_len, packet_space) and subtracts it from packet_space, out_len and in_len and adds it to tso->dma_addr. It computes eop as true when out_len, packet_space or segs_space is 0, then appends a descriptor to txq->pend_desc (incrementing n_pend_desc) with efx_tx_qdesc_dma_create using the saved (pre-update) dma_addr, length n and eop.
note: sfxge_tx.c:1150-1196 (the comment above it says it returns 0/1 but the function is void). Reviewer original right (FATSOV2 increments seqnum and leaves dma_addr unchanged); round 15 right (the descriptor uses the saved dma_addr from before adding n, 1155, 1195). Old prose wrongly implied all counters were decremented in both modes. No locking is done here.

name: sfxge_tx_init
prose: Initializes the transmit side of the sfxge driver; returns 0 or an errno. Precondition: the interrupt state is SFXGE_INTR_INITIALIZED (KASSERT). It first validates the tunables: sfxge_tx_dpl_get_max <= 0, sfxge_tx_dpl_get_non_tcp_max <= 0 or sfxge_tx_dpl_put_max < 0 each log a message and return EINVAL before any other state is changed (sc->txq_count is not reset on these returns). It then sets sc->txq_count = SFXGE_EVQ0_N_TXQ(sc) - 1 + intr.n_alloc, computes sc->tso_fw_assisted from the tunable minus the FATSOV1 and FATSOV2 bits the NIC does not support or has not enabled, and creates the 'txq' sysctl node (ENOMEM on failure, with txq_count set to 0). When sc->txq_dynamic_cksum_toggle_supported is false it initializes the NON_CKSUM and IP_CKSUM queues with sfxge_tx_qinit; it then initializes the IP_TCP_UDP_CKSUM queues, one per event queue. On success it calls sfxge_tx_stat_init and returns 0. If a queue init fails, the unwind frees the queues already initialized: after a TCP/UDP queue failure it finalizes the earlier TCP/UDP queues and then also the IP_CKSUM and NON_CKSUM queues, even when the dynamic toggle skipped initializing those two; a failure at the IP_CKSUM or NON_CKSUM init finalizes the earlier ones; failures after the txq_count assignment set txq_count to 0 and return the error.
note: sfxge_tx.c:1999-2087 (packet name correct; slice cut the head). Reviewer round 15 right (tunable EINVAL returns before txq_count assignment at 2031); round 17 right (the fail3 path finalizes IP_CKSUM and NON_CKSUM queues unconditionally, 2072-2079, even when the toggle-supported case never initialized them).

name: siis_timeout
prose: Callout handler for a command timeout on a SIIS slot; static void. Precondition: the channel mutex is held (mtx_assert). If the slot's state is below SIIS_SLOT_RUNNING it returns. If the command is an ATA control command with the reset bit (ATA_A_RESET) set, it freezes the SIM queue for ch->numrslots, ends the transaction with SIIS_ERR_TFE through siis_end_transaction and returns, without modifying ch->toslots itself (siis_end_transaction may clear this slot's bit). Otherwise it prints diagnostic register values and 'Timeout on slot', freezes the SIM queue once when ch->toslots was empty (xpt_freeze_simq(ch->sim, 1)), sets this slot's bit in ch->toslots, and if all running slots are now timed out ((ch->rslots & ~ch->toslots) == 0) calls siis_process_timeout(dev), else prints which slots it is still waiting for.
note: siis.c:1170-1206. Reviewer original right (soft-reset timeout path ends with SIIS_ERR_TFE and freezes the queue without setting toslots, 1183-1188); round 15 partly right: siis_end_transaction does touch toslots (1320-1321 clears the slot bit; I did not verify the condition around 1316-1321), so 'toslots untouched' was too strong. Not read: siis_end_transaction beyond that line, siis_process_timeout beyond its loop.

name: sk_intr_bcom
prose: Handles a Broadcom PHY interrupt for an SK network interface; static void. It clears the XMAC TX and RX enable bits in XM_MMUCMD, reads the PHY interrupt status register (BRGPHY_MII_ISR) to clear pending interrupts, and if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it calls sk_init_xmac(sc_if) and returns without setting the TX/RX enable bits again. Otherwise, only when the status has BRGPHY_ISR_LNK_CHG or BRGPHY_ISR_AN_PR set, it reads the aux status: if the link is down while sk_link was set it calls mii_mediachg, turns the link LED off and clears sk_link; else if LNK_CHG is set it writes the interrupt mask register 0xFF00, calls mii_tick, sets sk_link and turns the link LED on; else (AN_PR only) it calls mii_tick and reschedules the sk_tick callout in hz ticks. With neither status bit set it does none of that. At the end of the running path it sets the XMAC TX and RX enable bits again and returns.
note: if_sk.c:2880-2929. Reviewer original right (the not-running path returns after sk_init_xmac without restoring the enable bits, 2896-2899); round 15 right (the link handling only runs when LNK_CHG or AN_PR is set, 2901). Not read: sk_init_xmac, mii_tick bodies.

name: pqi_process_firmware_features
prose: Negotiates firmware features with the smartpqi controller through the PQI configuration table; static void, no return value. First pass over the local pqi_firmware_features[] list: an entry for PQI_FIRMWARE_FEATURE_UNIQUE_SATA_WWN is skipped (nothing recorded, no callback) when softs->sata_unique_wwn is not set; for every other entry, if the controller reports the feature as supported (pqi_is_firmware_feature_supported) it marks the entry supported and counts it; otherwise it logs a warning, calls pqi_firmware_feature_update for it and, if the entry is the PQI_FIRMWARE_FEATURE_MAX_KNOWN_FEATURE bit, stops scanning. If no feature is supported it returns. It then requests each supported feature in the firmware features table with pqi_request_firmware_feature, except that with DEVICE_HINT defined it skips features for which check_device_hint_status returns nonzero. It calls pqi_enable_firmware_features; if that fails it logs an error, calls pqi_firmware_feature_update for every supported entry and returns. Otherwise it checks each supported entry with pqi_is_firmware_feature_enabled: enabled ones get enabled = true, the others log a warning, and pqi_firmware_feature_update is called for each supported entry.
note: smartpqi_features.c:332-416. Reviewer original right (SATA-WWN entries skipped, scan breaks at MAX_KNOWN, early return when nothing is supported: 346-350, 364-366, 372-373); round 15 right (DEVICE_HINT skip at 379-382). Returns 373, 398, and the end. Not read: callee bodies.

name: pqisrc_sis_wait_for_db_bit_to_clear
prose: Waits for a doorbell bit to clear in the legacy SIS interface; returns PQI_STATUS_SUCCESS, PQI_STATUS_FAILURE or PQI_STATUS_TIMEOUT. It loops: it reads the host-to-IOA doorbell register (LEGACY_SIS_IDBR) and exits with success when (db_reg & bit) is 0; otherwise, if the firmware status shows PQI_CTRL_KERNEL_PANIC it logs and exits with PQI_STATUS_FAILURE; otherwise, once loop_cnt has reached SIS_DB_BIT_CLEAR_TIMEOUT_CNT (checked before each increment) it logs that the bit was not cleared and exits with PQI_STATUS_TIMEOUT; otherwise it sleeps 500 (OS_SLEEP(500)) and repeats. It returns the result code. No locks are taken.
note: smartpqi_sis.c:507-535 (packet name wait_for_db_bit_clear does not exist; real name pqisrc_sis_wait_for_db_bit_to_clear, so fixed instead of dropped). Returns single exit at 535. Not read: GET_FW_STATUS, OS_SLEEP, PCI_MEM_GET32.

name: pqisrc_get_tag
prose: Pops a free tag from the lock-free tag stack; returns the tag index or INVALID_ELEM. It compiles only when LOCKFREE_STACK is defined. It loops: it copies stack->head; if the head's top index is 0 (stack empty) it returns INVALID_ELEM; otherwise it builds a new head with seq_no incremented and index equal to stack->next_index_array[cur_head.top.index], and tries to install it with os_atomic64_cas on stack->head.data, retrying if the compare-and-swap fails. After a successful swap it sets next_index_array[cur_head.top.index] to 0, decrements stack->num_elem (a plain, non-atomic update) and returns cur_head.top.index.
note: smartpqi_tag.c:250-269 (packet name lockfree_stack_pop is the concept; the function is pqisrc_get_tag). The slice 254-271 starts in it. Returns 258 (INVALID_ELEM), 269. Not read: os_atomic64_cas.

name: smb_ioctl
prose: ioctl handler of the smb character device; returns 0 or an errno. It reads the smbcmd from data; if the device minor has bit 0x0400 set it overrides s->slave with the low 10 bits of the minor. It returns EINVAL if the slave address is odd (s->slave & 1). It requests the SMBus bus with smbus_request_bus (SMB_DONTWAIT for O_NONBLOCK, otherwise SMB_WAIT | SMB_INTR) and returns that error if nonzero. Under COMPAT_FREEBSD32 it first converts the 32-bit command structure into a local smbcmd for the *32 command codes. It then dispatches on cmd: quick write/read, send byte, receive byte (stores into s->cmd), write byte/word call the matching smbus_* call and convert the SMBus error with smbus_error; read byte, read word and process call, if their smbus call succeeded and s->rbuf is non-NULL with s->rcount large enough (1 or 2), copyout the 1 or 2 result bytes to s->rbuf (error from copyout kept) and set s->rcount to the size copied; block write returns EINVAL for a negative wcount, clamps wcount to SMB_MAXBLOCKSIZE, copies the data in (copyin error kept) and calls smbus_bwrite; block read returns EINVAL for a negative rcount, clamps it to SMB_MAXBLOCKSIZE, calls smbus_bread, shortens rcount to the byte count read and copies the data out; any other command gives ENOTTY. For compat 32-bit commands the results are copied back to the 32-bit structure: cmd for SMB_RECVB32; only rdata.word for the read-byte, read-word and process-call variants (not rcount); and rdata.word (when rbuf is NULL) plus rcount for SMB_BREAD32. It releases the bus with smbus_release_bus and returns the error, including after a failed smbus request (that path returns before the release).
note: smb.c:~190-415 (head at about 190; slice 256-420 starts inside). Reviewer round 17 right: the compat copy-back for READB/READW/PCALL copies only rdata.word (CP(*s,*s32,rdata.word) at 401), not rcount. Returns 217 (EINVAL), 222, 415. Not read: the smbus_* callee bodies; the head lines 185-195 not displayed.

name: smbus_error
prose: Converts an SMBus error bit mask to a unix errno; int. If smb_error equals SMB_ENOERR it returns 0. Otherwise it tests the bits in this order: SMB_ENOTSUPP gives ENODEV; else SMB_ENOACK gives ENXIO; else SMB_ETIMEOUT gives EWOULDBLOCK; else SMB_EBUSY gives EBUSY; else any of SMB_EABORT, SMB_EBUSERR or SMB_ECOLLI gives EIO; any other nonzero value gives EINVAL. When several bits are set the first match in that order wins.
note: smbconf.c:63-83. Returns 68 (0) and 83. No state is read or written.

name: atiixp_chan_trigger
prose: Trigger callback for an ATI IXP audio channel; static int, returns 0. If the trigger is not one of the common PCMTRIG start/stop/abort values (PCMTRIG_COMMON false) it returns 0 at once. Otherwise it takes the softc lock. PCMTRIG_START: flushes and rebuilds the scatter/gather table, writes the link pointer register (0 then the table address with ATI_REG_LINKPTR_EN) and enables the DMA; when sc->polling is nonzero it resets ch->ptr and prevptr, computes pollticks from hz, the block size and the buffer format (a quarter of the block period, clamped to between 1 and hz) and, only if no channel was running or pollticks is less than sc->poll_ticks, stores it in sc->poll_ticks and arms the poll timer callout; it then sets ATI_IXP_CHN_RUNNING. PCMTRIG_STOP and PCMTRIG_ABORT: disable and flush the DMA, clear ATI_IXP_CHN_RUNNING and, when polling, stop the poll timer and reset poll_ticks to 1 if no channel remains active, or recompute the tick count from the remaining running channel and, if it is larger than poll_ticks, store it and re-arm the timer. Any other trigger value unlocks and returns 0 without further work. For START, STOP and ABORT it then reads ATI_REG_IER and sets or clears ATI_REG_IER_SET_BUS_BUSY according to whether the command register has any of the send, receive or S/PDIF-out enable bits, writes it back, releases the lock and returns 0.
note: atiixp.c:718-820. Reviewer original right (START arms the poll timer only when polling and no active channel or shorter pollticks, 738-763); round 15 wrong: the ATI_REG_IER bus-busy update is present at 810-816. Returns 726, 806, 820.

name: emu_init
prose: Initializes an EMU10K1/Audigy sound chip (emu10k1.c); returns 0 or -1. It programs the hardware configuration and interrupt registers, clears the record buffer registers and the clean/solo interrupt enables, resets all NUM_G voice channel registers and the software voice table (vnum, slave, busy, etc.), sets pnum and rnum to 0, writes the default S/PDIF channel status word to EMU_SPCS0..2, and for non-Audigy chips calls emu_initefx (for Audigy 2 it also adjusts the S/PDIF sample-rate register and writes two port pairs). It initializes the page table: SLIST_INIT of mem.blocks, allocates ptb_pages (returning -1 if it fails) and a silent page (freeing ptb_pages and returning -1 if that allocation fails), fills every page table entry with the silent page address and sets EMU_PTB, EMU_TCB, EMU_TCBS and the per-voice map registers. It then enables audio: for Audigy chips it writes the HCFG value, calls audigy_initefx and sets audio enable and clears the GP output (Audigy 2 also unmutes analog); for the original EMU10K1 it writes HCFG with the audio-enable, lock-tank and auto-mute bits (plus joystick enable when sc->rev >= 6) and then probes the S/PDIF (TOS link) state: sc->tos_link is set to 0 and set to 1 only in this non-Audigy branch when the GP inputs indicate it and a probe write changes the register. It returns 0.
note: emu10k1.c:1744-1980 (slice 1807-2060 starts inside; packet name correct). Reviewer round 15 right: tos_link is assigned only in the non-Audigy branch (1968-1975). Returns 1887, 1893, 1980. PARTLY READ: register write sequences (1750-1830) skimmed, not verified individually.

name: emu_rate_to_pitch
prose: Converts a sample rate to an EMU10K2 pitch register value (emu10kx.c); static uint32_t. If rate is 0 it returns 0. Otherwise it multiplies rate by 11185 in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic (which wraps for rate above about 383990), then scans bit positions from 31 down to 1 for the first set bit of the shifted value, shifting it left each step. At the first set bit i it returns ((i - 15) << 20) + logMagTable[(rate >> 24) & 0x7f] + ((rate >> 17) & 0x7f) * logSlopeTable[(rate >> 24) & 0x7f], using the shifted value; if no bit from 31 down to 1 is set (for example when the product is 0 or has only bit 0 set) it returns 0. It uses two static tables of 128 entries and takes no locks.
note: emu10kx.c:1183-1236 (packet name correct; slice 1023-1282 contains the function). Reviewers round 2 and 15 right that the old prose examples (rates 3, 4, 5) did not match the code; examples removed. Return statements 1228-1231 and 1235. Table contents not checked.

name: envy24htchan_trigger
prose: Trigger callback for an Envy24HT PCM channel; returns 0 or -1 as error. It takes sc->lock and selects slot 0 for playback and 1 for record. PCMTRIG_START: if neither slot is running it sets the card speed with envy24ht_setspeed(ch->speed) and pins the min and max speed of both capability entries; otherwise a channel speed that is nonzero and differs from the card speed gives error -1 (goto fail); a zero channel speed takes the card speed. It increments run[slot]; for the first channel in the slot it resets ch->offset and sets blk[slot] = ch->blk, otherwise it computes ch->offset from the hardware pointer and lowers blk[slot] if ch->blk is smaller. For a playback channel it runs ch->emldma and envy24ht_setvolume; for both directions it calls envy24ht_updintr(sc, ch->dir) and, for the first running channel in the slot, envy24ht_start(sc, ch->dir); then sets ch->run = 1. PCMTRIG_EMLDMAWR and PCMTRIG_EMLDMARD require ch->run == 1 (else error -1) and call ch->emldma. PCMTRIG_ABORT, if the channel is running, clears ch->run, decrements run[slot], mutes the volume for playback, and when run[slot] reaches 0 calls envy24ht_stop(sc, ch->dir) and sets sc->intr[slot] = 0. Other values do nothing. It releases the lock at the fail label and returns the error.
note: envy24ht.c:1667-1773. Reviewer round 15 right: START calls updintr and start for record too (1719-1721 are outside the PLAY-only block), and ABORT also clears sc->intr[slot] (1755). Returns: single return at 1773.

name: fm801_wrcd
prose: Writes an AC97 codec register on an FM801 (ac97 write method); returns 0 or -1. Parameters: devinfo is the fm801_info, regno the codec register, data the 16-bit value to write. It first polls the FM_CODEC_CMD register's BUSY bit up to TIMO times with a 10 ms DELAY; if the codec is still busy it prints 'fm801 wrcd: read codec busy' and returns -1 without writing. Otherwise it writes data to FM_CODEC_DATA and regno to FM_CODEC_CMD (both 16-bit writes), then polls the BUSY bit again up to TIMO times with 10 ms delays; if it never clears it prints the same message and returns -1 (the write has already been issued), else it returns 0.
note: fm801.c:239-272. Reviewer round 15 wrong: the code does poll before the write (249-256) and again after (262-269), the old prose was right; reviewer round 2 right that data is the codec value, not a pointer; original reviewer right that -1 happens on a timeout (either poll). Returns 255, 268, 271.

name: tr_wrcd
prose: Writes an AC97 codec register on a Trident-family sound chip; returns 0 or -1. It selects the codec write register and busy-status bit by tr->type: SPA, ALI and TDX use their own register and status-bit constants and TNX adds the secondary-codec bit when bit 8 of regno is set; for any other type it prints '!!! tr_wrcd defaulted !!!' and returns -1 without touching hardware. It masks regno with 0x7f, takes tr->lock, and for the ALI chip polls the busy bit up to TR_TIMEOUT_CDC times and then, if the poll did not time out, reads register 0xc8 twice and polls until the two values differ (up to the timeout again). For non-ALI chips, or for ALI when the previous waits did not time out, it polls the busy bit again (up to TR_TIMEOUT_CDC reads); for an ALI chip with tr->rev above 0x01 it sets 0x0100 in the status mask, then it writes (data << TR_CDC_DATA) | regno | status-bit to the codec write register, even if that last poll timed out. It releases the lock, prints a timeout message when the poll counter reached 0 and returns 0 when the counter is above 0, else -1; so a timed-out last poll returns -1 although the write was issued, and an ALI chip whose first wait timed out returns -1 without writing.
note: t4dwave.c:238-296. Reviewer original right (ALI can poll up to three loops and still write after the last poll times out); round 2 right (-1 after the write when the final poll timed out); round 15 wrong: there is a default case at 257-259 that prints and returns -1 (unknown types are not written like non-ALI). Returns 259, 295.

name: chn_syncdestroy
prose: Removes a channel from its sync group if it has one; returns int. Precondition: the caller holds the sync group list mutex (PCM_SG_LOCKASSERT(MA_OWNED)). It starts with sg_id = 0. If c->sm is non-NULL it takes the member sm and its group sg, sets c->sm to NULL, removes the member from sg->members and frees it; if the group's member list is then empty it removes the group from the global snd_pcm_syncgroups list, records sg->id in sg_id and frees the group. It returns sg_id, which is non-zero only when the removed member was the last one of its group (so the caller can release the group id after dropping the lock), and 0 otherwise, including when c had no sync member.
note: channel.c:2543-2570 (packet name 'unnamed_syncgroup_teardown'). Single return at 2570. KASSERT(sg != NULL) is debug-only. Not read: SLIST macros beyond use.

name: dsp_oss_engineinfo
prose: Handler body for SNDCTL_ENGINEINFO: fills an oss_audioinfo for an audio engine (a channel) by index; returns 0 or EINVAL. If ai->dev is -1 and the ioctl came on a device that is not a dsp device (i_dev->si_devsw != &dsp_cdevsw) it returns EINVAL. It takes the bus topology lock and iterates over the registered pcm units (pcm_devclass), locking each device and walking its pcm channels with a running channel index nchan; for each channel it locks it and stops at the first channel for which either ai->dev is -1 and devfs_foreach_cdevpriv with dsp_oss_engineinfo_cb reports the channel as owned by the opened device, or ai->dev equals nchan; other channels are unlocked and counted. When a channel was found it zeroes *ai and fills it: ai->dev is the channel index nchan (not the pcm unit), name, busy state (OPEN_WRITE or OPEN_READ when the channel is busy), pid and command, capability flags, the natively supported formats (stored in oformats for playback and iformats for record) and the minimum and maximum channel counts from the channel caps, card_number, port_number and legacy_device set to the pcm unit, mixer_dev (the unit when the device has a mixer, else -1), /dev/dsp<unit> as devnode, enabled from device_is_attached, min and max rates (from the capabilities for an exclusive or bitperfect channel, else from feeder_rate_min and feeder_rate_max), the rates list from chn_getrates limited to OSS_MAX_SAMPLE_RATES, and next_play_engine and next_rec_engine as 0. It then unlocks the channel and device, releases the bus topology lock and returns 0. If no channel matched in any unit it releases the bus topology lock and returns EINVAL. This function has no 'unavailable' branch.
note: dsp.c:2300-2480 (packet name dsp_oss_audioinfo is a different function at 2119; the slice 2316-2566 is dsp_oss_engineinfo). Reviewer round 15 right: ai->dev is set to nchan (2368) and there is no unavailable path (the unavail helper belongs to dsp_oss_audioinfo). Returns 2314, 2475, 2480.

name: z_resampler_set
prose: Sets a resampler feeder parameter and re-runs the setup; static int. what selects FEEDRATE_SRC, FEEDRATE_DST, FEEDRATE_QUALITY or FEEDRATE_CHANNELS; any other value returns EINVAL. For SRC and DST a value outside feeder_rate_min..feeder_rate_max returns E2BIG; a value equal to the current rsrc or rdst returns 0 unchanged; otherwise the field is changed. For QUALITY a value outside Z_QUALITY_MIN..Z_QUALITY_MAX returns EINVAL, an unchanged value returns 0, otherwise the quality is changed and z_resampler_setup(f) is called: if that returns 0 the function returns 0, if it fails the old quality is restored and the function falls through to the final call, so it then returns the result of z_resampler_setup(f) with the old quality (which may be 0). For CHANNELS a value outside SND_CHN_MIN..SND_CHN_MAX returns EINVAL, an unchanged value returns 0, else the channel count is changed. For SRC, DST and CHANNELS the new value stays stored even when the final z_resampler_setup(f) returns an error, and that error is returned.
note: feeder_rate.c:1386-1437. Reviewer original right (quality setup failure restores the old value then retries and may return 0; the other fields stay changed on setup failure); round 15 right (unknown `what` returns EINVAL, 1432-1433, so it is not a precondition). Not read: z_resampler_setup (1054-1384).

name: mixer_setrecsrc
prose: Selects the recording source of a mixer; static int. It gets the sound device d = device_get_softc(mixer->dev); if d is NULL it returns -1. It decides whether it must drop the mixer lock: dropmtx is 1 when the device is not SD_F_MPSAFE and the mixer lock is currently owned by the caller, else 0 (so the lock need not be held). It masks src with mixer->recdevs; if the result is 0 it tries in order the microphone, monitor and line bits of recdevs, and if still 0 while recdevs is non-zero it uses the lowest set bit of recdevs. It then releases the mixer lock (when dropmtx), calls MIXER_SETRECSRC(mixer, src) to let the driver apply it, retakes the lock (when dropmtx), stores the driver's returned mask in mixer->recsrc and returns 0.
note: mixer.c:334-363. Reviewer original right (the lock handling is conditional on ownership, 343-346); round 15 right (NULL softc returns -1 at 341-342). Returns 342, 363. Not read: MIXER_SETRECSRC callee.

name: ste_intr
prose: Interrupt handler of the Sundance ST201 (ste) Ethernet driver; static void. It takes STE_LOCK. With DEVICE_POLLING defined and IFCAP_POLLING enabled it unlocks and returns before reading any status. Otherwise it reads STE_ISR_ACK (acknowledging the status); if IFF_DRV_RUNNING is not set it unlocks and returns without servicing events and without rewriting STE_IMR. If the status is 0xFFFF or has no bit in STE_INTRS it jumps to the end (the label inside the running block) and rewrites STE_IMR with the current mask, without servicing any event. Otherwise, if Rx interrupt moderation is active (ste_int_rx_act > 0) it drops the Rx-DMA-done bit from the status and mask; for a SOFTINTR or RX_DMADONE status it calls ste_rxeof(sc, -1) and, if still running with ste_int_rx_mod nonzero, arms the countdown timer and masks Rx-DMA-done (setting ste_int_rx_act = 1) or, when the status did not carry RX_DMADONE, unmasks it and clears ste_int_rx_act. While still running it then handles TX_DMADONE (ste_txeof), TX_DONE (ste_txeoc) and STATS_OFLOW (ste_stats_update); a HOSTERR status clears IFF_DRV_RUNNING, calls ste_init_locked, unlocks and returns without re-enabling interrupts here; otherwise it starts transmission with ste_start_locked when the send queue is non-empty, writes the interrupt mask register STE_IMR with the updated mask and unlocks.
note: if_ste.c:504-582 (slice 510-761 starts inside; packet name correct). Reviewer round 15 right (DEVICE_POLLING path returns before STE_ISR_ACK is read, 514-518; the no-interrupt or 0xFFFF path rewrites STE_IMR without servicing events, 528-529, 577-579). Returns 517, 524, 573 and the end. Not read: the helper bodies.

name: sym_prepare_setting
prose: Computes the SCSI controller's software settings from its features, saved registers and NVRAM; static int, returns 0 (its only return statement). It sets np->maxwide from FE_WIDE; the clock multiplier (4 for FE_QUAD, 2 for FE_DBLR, else 1) and clock_khz (40 or 80 MHz times the multiplier, calling sym_getclock when it is not 40000); the SCNTL3 value from the divider table (zeroed on FE_C10); minsync and maxsync from the clock, raised to at least 25 or 12 depending on the Ultra feature bits; the DT sync limits for FE_C10|FE_ULTRA3 at 160 MHz; the CCNTL0/CCNTL1 flags from FE_DAC and FE_NOPM and an erratum on the 53C1010; the burst length from the saved registers and limits; the DMODE, DCNTL, CTEST3, CTEST4, CTEST5 and SCNTL0 bits from the features and the setup options (parity checking, prefetch, cache-line, write-and-invalidate), clearing FE_WRIE, FE_ERL and FE_ERMP for a 53C810 erratum case; the host SCSI id (from the NVRAM or the SCID register, default SYM_SETUP_HOST_ID); the SCSI mode (single-ended or differential, setting the HVD bit); the LED feature; the IRQ mode bit; and for every target the default user period, offset and width, with FE_ULTRA3 DT-capable limits, and tags. It prints the controller summary when sym_verbose is set and returns 0.
note: sym_hipd.c:2467-2794 (slice 2550-2808 starts inside and also includes the head of sym_prepare_nego; packet name 'unnamed chip-setup function'). Return at 2794. PARTLY READ: only control-flow and assignment lines of 2476-2790 were read; individual register bit values, the NVRAM handling (2640-2660) and the erratum conditions were not verified.

name: daemon_saver
prose: Screen-saver callback that draws a bouncing daemon picture and moving host-name text; returns 0 or EAGAIN. It finds the softc with sc_find_softc (EAGAIN if NULL) and uses sc->cur_scp. If blank is non-zero: in a graphics video mode (V_INFO_GRAPHICS) it returns EAGAIN; on the first call (blanked == 0) it clears the screen text buffer, hides the hardware cursor, sets the border to black and zeroes the clip lengths; it returns 0 for the first two calls (blanked++ < 2) and then sets blanked = 1. On later calls it erases the previously drawn daemon and string (clear_daemon, clear_string). The daemon position moves only on every other call: moved_daemon is pre-incremented and the movement block runs when the result is non-zero (the block sets moved_daemon back to -1). In that block it computes min and max for the x position from the screen width (when the screen is not wider than the picture it uses min = xsize - DAEMON_MAX_WIDTH - 10 and max = 10, so positions may be negative), flips dxdir at the limits, does the same for y, advances dxpos and dypos by their directions and computes the x and y offsets and lengths: a position at or beyond the screen edge gives length 0, a negative position sets the offset to -pos and a position that overruns the screen edge shortens the length; the offset is not subtracted from the length. Every call (not only on movement) updates the message position txpos/typos with the same kind of clamping and clipping (toff, tlen) and then draws the daemon and the string. If blank is 0 it sets blanked to 0. It returns 0.
note: daemon_saver.c:204-348 (slice 268-390 starts inside; name correct). Reviewer original right (negative positions can give xlen/ylen larger than the visible part after the offset: 289-306 do not subtract the offset from the length); round 15 right (min can be negative, 254, 269). Returns 219, 224, 234, 348. Not read: draw_daemon, clear_daemon, draw_string.

name: gfb_cursor
prose: Draws, moves or hides the text cursor on a generic framebuffer console; static void. Two variants exist in the file. Variant for SC_OFWFB builds: if scp->curs_attr.height <= 0 (cursor disabled) it returns without changing any status; with blink set it sets VR_CURSOR_BLINK, and when on is set sets VR_CURSOR_ON and moves the hardware cursor to at (column at % xsize, row at / xsize), otherwise hides the hardware cursor if VR_CURSOR_ON was set and clears VR_CURSOR_ON; without blink it clears VR_CURSOR_BLINK and, when on is set, sets VR_CURSOR_ON, redraws the character at cursor_oldpos from the screen buffer and draws the character at position at with swapped foreground and background nibbles (an inverse-video cursor by software), or when on is clear and VR_CURSOR_ON was set redraws the character at at normally and clears VR_CURSOR_ON. Other builds: after the same disabled-cursor early return, if on is set and blink is 0 it sets VR_CURSOR_ON and positions the hardware cursor at at; if on is set with blink it increments pxlblinkrate and, when bit 2 of it is set, resets it, toggles VR_CURSOR_ON and moves the hardware cursor to at or hides it (-1, -1); if on is clear it moves the hardware cursor to at when VR_CURSOR_ON was set and clears VR_CURSOR_ON; finally it sets or clears VR_CURSOR_BLINK according to blink. The flip argument is unused.
note: scgfbrndr.c:212-251 (SC_OFWFB variant) and 253-287 (other variant). Reviewer original right (disabled cursor returns early without updating status bits, 219-220, 260-262); round 15 right (the #else variant uses the hardware cursor, blink handled via pxlblinkrate). The packet's slice contains both variants.

name: scsplash_saver
prose: Screen-saver callback that shows or removes the splash image (DEV_SPLASH); static void. It uses a static busy flag: if busy is already TRUE it returns immediately without touching it; otherwise it sets busy to TRUE, works on sc->cur_scp and sets busy to FALSE at the end, so every path after the first check clears it. With show set and SC_SAVER_FAILED not set it blanks the screen (set_scrn_saver_mode) if the screen is not already blanked and calls splash(sc->adp, TRUE): result 0 does nothing more; EAGAIN restores the saver mode (restore_scrn_saver_mode(scp, FALSE)) and touches the screen saver timer, without setting SC_SAVER_FAILED; any other result sets SC_SAVER_FAILED, clears the sticky splash, restores the mode (restore_scrn_saver_mode(scp, TRUE)) and prints 'scsplash_saver(): failed to put up the image'. With show clear and the splash not sticky, if the screen is blanked and splash(sc->adp, FALSE) returns 0 it restores the saver mode with TRUE. busy is cleared after those cases.
note: syscons.c:2454-2490 (slice 2378-2628 starts earlier). Reviewer original right (EAGAIN restores the mode without SC_SAVER_FAILED, 2471-2474); round 15 right that the early busy return (2459-2460) leaves busy set (it was set by another caller), so 'busy is cleared before every return' was wrong. Returns 2460, end. Not read: splash(), set_scrn_saver_mode, restore_scrn_saver_mode bodies.

name: sc_switch_scr
prose: Requests a switch to another virtual terminal; returns 0 or an errno. If sc->cur_scp is NULL it returns 0. If SC_SCRN_VTYLOCK is set it rings the bell and returns EPERM. If the screen is blanked or a write or blink is in progress it records delayed_next_scr = next_scr + 1, touches the screen saver and returns 0 (the switch is delayed); otherwise it clears delayed_next_scr and raises spl. While a switch is already in progress and the current vty is in VT_PROCESS mode with a controlling process, it checks whether that process died: if so a pending WAIT_REL finishes the previous switch with finish_vt_rel(TRUE) and returns EINVAL, a pending WAIT_ACQ is completed with finish_vt_acq and execution continues, otherwise it only logs; if the process is alive but not answering, in WAIT_REL the switch_in_progress counter is incremented and on the fourth and later calls it forces finish_vt_rel(FALSE) and returns EINVAL (the second call resends the release signal), and in WAIT_ACQ it resends the acquire signal on the second call and forces finish_vt_acq on the fourth and later. It then returns EINVAL (with a bell) if next_scr is outside first_vty..first_vty+vtys or a switch is still in progress; EINVAL for leaving a graphics-mode VT_AUTO vty that is open, unless the target is the same vty; EINVAL if the target is not the kernel console and its tty is not open; EINVAL if the debugger is active and the target is not the console and is in VT_PROCESS mode (this check is skipped when next_scr is the console vty). It then sets switch_in_progress, old_scp and new_scp; if both are the same it clears switch_in_progress, wakes up waiters unless kdb_active and returns 0. Otherwise it signals the old vty's release (returning 0 if the process must answer first), exchanges screens with exchange_scr, wakes up waiters unless kdb_active, signals acquisition (returning 0 if the process must answer), and otherwise clears switch_in_progress, announces console availability when this is the console unit and returns 0.
note: syscons.c:2664-2891 (packet slice starts inside; name correct). Reviewer original right (EINVAL for kdb_active and VT_PROCESS target at 2830-2834; the forced WAIT_REL resets return EINVAL as listed, WAIT_ACQ ones continue); round 15 right (that kdb check sits inside the `next_scr != console` test, 2822-2836, so it is skipped for the kernel console). Not read: exchange_scr, finish_vt_*, signal_vt_*.

name: ns8250_divisor
prose: Computes the 16-bit baud rate divisor for an 8250-family UART; static int. It returns 0 if baudrate is 0. Otherwise divisor = (rclk / (baudrate << 3) + 1) >> 1, i.e. rclk / (16 * baudrate) rounded, and it returns 0 if the divisor is 0 or at least 65536. It computes actual_baud = rclk / (divisor << 4) and the error in percent as (((actual_baud - baudrate) * 2000 / baudrate) + 1) / 2 (a rounded percentage), returning 0 if the error is below -UART_DEV_TOLERANCE_PCT or above UART_DEV_TOLERANCE_PCT. Otherwise it returns the divisor. It reads and writes no global state; the multiplications and the shift use int arithmetic, so large rclk or baudrate values can overflow.
note: uart_dev_ns8250.c:165-186. Returns 171, 175, 183, 185. Reviewer round 1 right (the returns of 0 for baudrate 0, invalid divisor or excessive error); round 15 about purity right (no side effects). Contract left empty (overflow and division behaviour not formalised).

name: ufshci_pci_setup_interrupts
prose: Chooses and sets up the controller's interrupt scheme (MSI-X, then MSI, then INTx); static int, returns 0 or an errno. With the tunable hw.ufshci.force_intx set it goes straight to INTx. If the device reports no MSI-X vectors it goes to MSI. Otherwise it derives num_io_queues from the tunables (hw.ufshci.num_io_queues clamped to 1..mp_ncpus, per_cpu_io_queues, min_cpus_per_ioq) and the available vector count minus one, rounds it down to a multiple of vm_ndomains when larger, and requests min(num_io_queues + 1, MSI-X count) vectors. If pci_alloc_msix fails it logs, clears msi_count and falls back to MSI. If exactly 1 vector was granted it returns ufshci_pci_setup_shared(ctrlr, 1) (which can return ENOMEM or the bus_setup_intr error); if a different number than requested was granted it releases the MSI, sets num_io_queues to granted - 1 and retries the request; when the request was granted in full it sets num_io_queues and returns 0 without installing any handler here (the multi-vector handlers are installed elsewhere). The MSI path requests min(MSI count, 2) MSIs: a failure clears msi_count and falls to INTx; a grant of 2 sets num_io_queues = 1 and returns 0 without installing a handler; otherwise it falls to the INTx step, which returns ufshci_pci_setup_shared(ctrlr, rid) with rid 1 when MSI count is above 0 and rid 0 otherwise.
note: ufshci_pci.c:178-260. Reviewer original right (nonzero return from ufshci_pci_setup_shared at 233 and 260); round 15 right (multi-vector MSI-X/MSI paths return 0 at 241 and 255 without installing a handler, and a short MSI-X grant is retried, 234-237). Not read: pci_alloc_msix semantics, ufshci_pci_setup_shared beyond 152-175.

name: dwc_otg_data_tx
prose: Device-mode (peripheral) IN data transmit step for a dwc_otg endpoint; static uint8_t returning 0 for complete and 1 for not complete. It loops at most 3 times (to starts at 3). For endpoint 0 with a pending last RX status for channel 0: a packet status that is neither SETUP data nor SETUP complete is acknowledged with dwc_otg_common_rx_ack; otherwise the transfer was cancelled by the host, td->error_any is set to 1 and it returns 0. If td->tx_bytes is non-zero it reads DIEPTSIZ to find how many packets the FIFO has consumed, computes the space left (up to max_buffer, or one max-size packet when max_buffer is 0), copies up to that many bytes into the FIFO with dwc_otg_write_fifo and updates tx_bytes, remainder, offset and npkt; if bytes are still pending it returns 1; if remainder is 0 and the transfer was short it returns 0 (complete). If the repeat budget is used up it returns 1. If DIEPTSIZ still shows packets pending it returns 1. Otherwise it programs the next burst: with a nonzero max_buffer and a max packet size multiple of 4 it computes the packet count (limited to min(max_buffer / max_packet_size, 0x3FE) and a byte count up to 0x7FFFFF) and sets short_pkt for a trailing short or zero-length packet; else it sends one packet; it writes DIEPTSIZ, flips the data PID bit for isochronous endpoints, writes DIEPCTL with EPENA and CNAK, sets tx_bytes to the byte count, and returns 0 if no bytes and no remainder are left and the packet was short, else repeats. The early returns (cancel, still-pending, not-complete) skip the DIEPTSIZ and DIEPCTL programming.
note: dwc_otg.c:2127-2312. Returns 2159, 2207 (complete), 2305 (complete), 2312 (not complete). Reviewer round 15 right (early returns skip DIEPTSIZ/DIEPCTL programming; no DIEPCTL write on every path); original reviewer right that the old annotation omitted return values and side effects. PARTLY READ: lines 2140-2163 (rx status check) skimmed.

name: dwc_otg_update_host_transfer_schedule_locked
prose: Re-schedules host-mode transfers when a new (micro)frame has started; static uint8_t returning 0 if HFNUM is unchanged from sc_last_frame_num and 1 otherwise. It reads the frame number (masked) and returns 0 if it equals sc_last_frame_num; else it stores it. When (frame & 7) == 0 it clears the TT info and walks the transfer queue (intr_q) in passes, moving each newly scheduled transfer to a temporary list and recording its start slot: isochronous transfers with a split (hcsplt != 0) not yet scheduled, first those whose direction is not IN (isochronous IN endpoints are skipped in that pass, and only scheduled if dwc_otg_compute_isoc_rx_tt_slot gives a slot <= 3), then those that are IN (start slot = frame); then interrupt transfers (subject to dwc_otg_host_rate_check_interrupt; those without a split are only flagged scheduled); then control transfers. Then, for (frame & 7) < 6, it does the same for bulk transfers. Each pass sets sc_needsof = 1 for the transfers it examines. It then, for every new frame, appends the temporary list to the queue, reorders the queue so entries with a split (hcsplt != 0) come first, and moves entries without a split that are not isochronous to the end. When (frame & 7) == 0 it finally adjusts the SOF interrupt mask: if SOFMSK is set and sc_needsof is 0 it clears the bit, if it is clear and sc_needsof is non-zero it sets it, writes GINTMSK in either case, and resets sc_needsof to 0. It returns 1.
note: dwc_otg.c:2488-2673. Reviewer original right (the first isochronous pass skips EPDIR_IN transfers, 2516-2517; IN ones are handled in the second pass 2541-2559); round 15 wrong in effect: the queue reordering (2633-2651) is outside the (frame & 7) == 0 block and runs for every new frame, as the old prose said. Returns 2500, 2673.

name: dwc_otg_interrupt
prose: Interrupt handler of the dwc_otg USB controller; static void. It takes the USB bus lock and spin lock, reads GINTSTS and writes back status & DWC_OTG_MSK_GINT_THREAD_IRQ to clear only the thread-level interrupt bits (other status bits are not cleared by this write). It then handles: GINTSTS_USBRST (sets device-mode and connect-change flags, clears the SOF interrupt mask and notifies the root hub); GINTSTS_ENUMDONE (marks the bus reset ended, reinitializes the FIFOs for device mode, sets address 0, records the enumerated speed, disables resume and SOF interrupts, enables suspend and notifies the root hub); GINTSTS_PRTINT (reads HPRT, writes back the HPRT change bits together with sc_hprt_val, updates the flags for connection, enable, over-current, power and speed, calls dwc_otg_suspend_irq or dwc_otg_resume_irq, notifies the root hub and updates the host frame interval); GINTSTS_WKUPINT (resume) or else GINTSTS_USBSUSP (suspend); and, when any of USBSUSP, USBRST, OTG or SESSREQ is set, reads GOTGCTL and calls dwc_otg_vbus_interrupt with whether a session is valid. Finally, if sc_xfer_complete is non-zero it clears it and calls dwc_otg_interrupt_complete_locked(sc). It releases both locks and returns void. Status bits outside these cases are only read, not acted on.
note: dwc_otg.c:2902-3082. Reviewer original right (only the listed bits are handled); round 15 right (the clearing write is status & DWC_OTG_MSK_GINT_THREAD_IRQ, 2914, i.e. not 'only thread-level status bits handled' but only those cleared).

name: ehci_non_isoc_done
prose: Completes a non-isochronous EHCI transfer; static void. It takes the QH for the current DMA set and invalidates its page cache, then starts from xfer->td_transfer_first. For a control transfer with a header stage it processes that stage with ehci_non_isoc_done_sub (its error kept), sets aframes to 1 and jumps to done if the transfer descriptor cache became NULL. It then loops over the data frames while aframes != nframes, calling ehci_non_isoc_done_sub for each, incrementing aframes and jumping to done if the descriptor cache became NULL. If it is a control transfer without an active data stage (control_act clear) it processes the status stage with ehci_non_isoc_done_sub. At done it calls ehci_device_done(xfer, err) with the last error code. The function itself invalidates the QH page cache, so the caller does not need to do that; the err of earlier frames is overwritten by later ones.
note: ehci.c:1190-1240. Reviewer original right (the function invalidates the QH page cache itself, 1210); round 15 right (the goto done when td_transfer_cache is NULL, 1222-1223, 1230-1231, skips remaining frames and the status stage). Not read: ehci_non_isoc_done_sub beyond its listing (1093-1187), ehci_device_done.

name: musbotg_host_ctrl_status_rx
prose: Host-mode control transfer IN status stage for the MUSB controller; static uint8_t, returns 0 for complete and 1 for not yet complete. It allocates a channel when td->channel is -1 (musbotg_channel_alloc) and returns 1 if none is available. It selects endpoint 0 (EPINDEX). On the first call (transaction_started clear) it programs the device address, hub address and port and the transfer type, sets the NAK limit, marks the transaction started, disables PING in RXCSRH and writes TXCSRL with the STATUSPKT and REQPKT bits, then returns 1. On later calls it reads TXCSRL: if RXPKTRDY is set it clears it, frees the channel and returns 0; if the NAK-timeout bit is set it clears the STATUSPKT and REQPKT and NAKTIMO bits (two writes) and sets td->error = 1; if the RXSTALL or ERROR bit is set it writes TXCSRL = 0 and sets td->error = 1. Then, if td->error is non-zero (set now or earlier, even when none of the bits above are set), it frees the channel and returns 0; otherwise it returns 1.
note: musb_otg.c:1276-1358 (packet name correct; slice starts inside). Reviewer round 15 right: a nonzero td->error from an earlier call with no error bits now still frees the channel and returns 0 (1353-1355). Returns 1289, 1319, 1330, 1355, 1358.
